To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the majority of children with asthma have atopic asthma; (2) atopic asthma is characterized by an IgE-mediated response to aeroallergens and/or foods; (3) the most common aeroallergen triggers of atopic asthma are dust mites, animal dander, cockroach, mold, and pollen; and (4) the most common food triggers of atopic food asthma are milk, eggs, wheat, soy, and peanuts.
